subject: frog
pitch: A red-eyed tree frog clinging to a leaf. Vivid lime-green skin, blue and cream striped flanks, orange toes with round sticky pads, a creamy white belly, and enormous ruby-red eyes with black slit pupils. It looks a little surprised, as if you just woke it up.
reasoning:
I'm scaling the model to a realistic red-eyed tree frog size, around 6-7cm body length, and planning to include a leaf as scenery so the frog and its perch both rest naturally at floor level.

Working out the leaf geometry now, I'm extruding a pointed ellipse outline in the horizontal XZ plane with the thickness running vertically so it sits flat as a perch, positioning it so its bottom edge just touches y=0.

Still writing leaf geometry...

For the frog body I'm planning to use scaled sphere primitives mounted on a simple joint skeleton, starting with hip and spine joints positioned along a short vertical arc above the leaf.

For the actual geometry, I'm sizing a body sphere and a slightly wider head sphere positioned near the front, then thinking through a paint function that paints lateral stripes along the flanks in blue and cream against a lime green base, with countershading to lighten the belly.

For the eyes, I'm placing large red spheres bulging out near the top of the head, then adding a flattened black slit for the pupil positioned just in front of each eye, scaling it to look vertical and narrow like a real tree frog's pupil.

Since parts place in world/model space without extra orientation, the bone attachment keeps it rigid as the head moves. Now I'm moving on to building the four limbs with proper toes.

For the hind legs, I'm figuring out hip placement and foot targets so they rest on the leaf surface, checking that the reach distance between hip and target is achievable given thigh and shin lengths. I'm considering whether to use a two-segment limb with a knee bend for simplicity, placing small toe spheres separately at the ankle rather than complicating the limb with a sole option.

I'm setting up the leg chain structure with named joints (hip, knee, ankle) and a tip, assigning it a "leg" role, then adding four fanned-out toes with orange pad spheres at the foot tip. Now I'm working out similar placement logic for the shorter front legs, positioning the shoulder and foot target further forward on the leaf.

Then I'm checking the reach distance between shoulder and target to ensure the limb lengths can span it without overextending, adjusting positions and bone lengths to fit within range, and planning out the spine joints (hips, chest, head) with parent relationships before attaching a sphere mesh to the chest joint for the body.

I'm now working out concrete coordinates for the frog's body, placing the body sphere so its bottom edge sits just above the leaf surface, setting foot pad targets low enough to touch near the leaf top, and defining hips, chest, and head joint positions with proper parenting and orientation.

For the eyes, I'm computing their position relative to the head joint using local left/up/forward offsets, checking that the eye spheres bulge appropriately out of the sides and front of the head sphere without being fully buried or floating too far out.

I'm setting explicit eye coordinates with ruby-red color, pupil placement with depth scaling, and a small white highlight dot for sparkle. For the mouth I'm sweeping a catmull curve across the front of the head to form a simple smile line, then planning orange toe pads and flank stripe placement using model-space x-coordinates to mirror across the body.

Working through the flank stripe logic, I decide longitudinal bands along the z-axis fit the red-eyed tree frog look better than transverse ones, so I'm defining a paint function that checks y-position bands on the sides to assign blue and cream stripes against the green base, then layering a countershade for the cream belly.

For the leaf, I'm planning a flat-colored paint with a lighter midrib vein running along the center, using the extruded outline coordinates to position it, and setting up the leaf extrusion so the frog's hind feet and toe pads can rest naturally on top.

I'm now working through the vertical stacking math carefully: leaf thickness and position (top surface around 0.005), toe pad centers sitting just above that, and body sphere center around 0.034 so legs connect properly. I'm checking that the lowest point of the whole model (leaf bottom near 0.001) stays within the 2% tolerance for a roughly 0.07-tall model, then moving to recompute all body-centered positions from there.

Now I'm defining the skeleton joints — hips, chest, and head — building up the chain from the pelvis. For the hind limb, I'm placing the hip socket, calculating the distance to a target foot position to confirm the leg segment lengths can reach it with a bend, and reasoning about which direction the knee hint vector should point so the knee bends outward and upward like a frog's, trying out candidate hint values for left/right symmetry.

Writing limb code...

I'm sketching out the toe fan directions for the hind feet so each toe radiates outward and backward from the ankle tip, then planning similar fan toes for the front feet pointing forward, using mirrored x-offsets for left/right symmetry. I'm also deciding on bone attachment (using the chain's tip joint) so toes and pads move rigidly with the foot, and thinking through eye placement, pupil slits, and highlight spheres on the head for the oversized red-eyed tree frog look, plus a thin mouth line swept along the head.

Writing frog build code...

Still writing limb and toe code...

Now I'm finalizing joint roles (spine for hips/chest, head for head, leg/arm for the limb chains), sweeping body coat colors over the limbs and torso spheres, and assembling the leaf extrusion with a vein-colored midrib before returning the completed rig as the final code output.
